runs.name: NextEra Energy, Inc.; NYSE NEE, SEC CIK 0000753308, 10-K filer jointly with Florida Power & Light Company; two principal businesses, FPL, the largest electric utility in Florida and the U.S., and NEER, long-term contracted generation, storage and transmission; formerly FPL Group, Inc., renamed 2010; merger agreement with Dominion Energy signed 2026-05-15 (0.8138 NEE shares and a pro rata share of $360M cash per Dominion share), voted at the special meeting 2026-09-03, not closed; the 10-K names no rival company, Duke, Southern and Dominion chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$81.90** (close 2026-10-22, aggregator, flagged). Shares 2,097,306,049 (10-Q cover 2026-09-30, 0000753308-26-000081, agreed with the filed balance sheet; cover_shares.py's 1,000 FPL shares, all held by NEE, not added); market cap $171,769M. Sovereign **5.29%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-22. Read from the 10-K FY2025 (0000753308-26-000015, NEE and FPL combined), the 10-Ks for FY2024, FY2023, FY2022 and FY2021, the 10-Q for 2026-09-30 (0000753308-26-000081), the proxy of 2026-04-01 (0001104659-26-038551), the merger 8-K (0001104659-26-063001), the joint proxy/prospectus of 2026-07-28 (0001104659-26-087576), the special-meeting 8-K (0000753308-26-000071) and the derivative-settlement 8-K (0000753308-26-000074); lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7; tools/run.py UNRESEARCHED, every figure from the filed statements. Run from scratch by one dispatched analyst. **Q1 IN** on FPL, the deciding part (72.9% of five-year net income attributable, $21,014M of $28,811M); rate agreement through 2029, allowed ROE 10.95% (band 9.95% to 11.95%), equity ratio 59.6%; NEER's growth economics recorded as outside foresight, NEER not deciding. **Q2 IN** on FPL: 226 franchises, typically 30 years, expiring through 2055; the regulator's return carried to Q3 as a second best; NEER's own words "commodity-driven" and "primarily competes on the basis of price", carried at no growth; the 10-K names no rival, Duke, Southern and Dominion chosen as a CONVENTION of the run; five-year return on book equity FPL 10.9%, Duke 7.4%, Southern 12.0%, Dominion 6.5%. **Q3 weighs for** on FPL as a second best, **against** on NEER and the whole: owner cash after all spending negative every year, -$5.8B to -$11.0B after asset sales; NEER growth capital about 4.1% in cash. **Q4 no STOP, weighs against**: ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025, debt $30.7B to $95.6B ($113.9B at 2026-09-30), common equity 2.2 times with about a third from issued shares, noncontrolling interests $1.0B to $11.9B (tax-equity partners), debt to common equity 1.26 to 1.85; about 56% of NEER's attributable income book losses allocated to tax-equity partners, FPL earnings steered to a target ROE by a reserve, adjusted earnings in pay and messaging. **Q5 OUT on integrity, on doubt [M2013-088]**: campaign-finance and "dark money" allegations about how FPL sought political outcomes (from 2021); the securities class action dismissed, revived by the 11th Circuit November 2025, being settled for $150M, insurance-paid; derivative actions naming the present chief executive being settled with nine political-oversight reforms (hearing 2026-12-14); the defendants deny all of it, no violation found in the filings read; the analyst notes another analyst could weigh it instead and would reach Q7, where no case earns the floor. Q6 to Q12 not reached. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash equity-only (read as central under Q7, The regulated utility, for a company of two parts; the reading flagged for the operator) after maintenance, stock pay and distributions to tax-equity partners 2021 to 2025 2,806 / 3,101 / 4,796 / 6,193 / 4,058 ($M), **$4,191M a year**; after all spending -$4,406M a year; value range **$25.45 to $37.77 a share** equity-only (the growth bought worth less than it costs, so no growth is the top), literal-window growth case $50.69 beside; 2.4% to 2.7% at the price (3.7% at the outermost bound); fair price **$11.53** equity-only, -$33.00 all-equity (not positive), -$6.13 on a sum-of-parts reading; the signed unclosed Dominion merger beside, as if closed, no growth, $44.62 a share, about 716M new shares, Dominion's owner cash bought at about 23 times against NEE's 41; termination fee $6.52B, or $4.83B on certain regulatory failures; XPLR stake written down $2.7B 2023 to 2025; dividends paid from borrowing and issued shares. Disclosed by the analyst: the owner-cash arithmetic and rough Q7 lines were run before Q5 was written, declared in the self-audit. Commits 7904fae8 (template), 8b9ed537 (Step 0, Q1), 1055802a (Q2), c61d4036 (Q3), 02a0a6ff (Q4), d69c8c28 (Q5 OUT), a38053ad (after the stop), 8b41d773 (close). No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the regulated-utility paragraph does not say how to read a company of two parts; at NEE the three readings give fair $11.53, -$6.13 and -$33.00; (2) the debt credit has no rule for the no-growth case; (3) tax-equity money is not addressed; (4) Whose tax does not fit a fleet whose credits are renewed by building, not applied, the figures high on that point; (5) Q2's parts threshold says operating profit where NEE reports segment net income only; (6) Q5's doubt rule meets unresolved litigation without guidance; (7) specific (e) gives no method for growth spending charged against the growth it buys; (8) the maintenance guess where D&A is net of a regulatory reserve. runs.narr: OUT at Q5 (NextEra Energy, NEE; FPL, the largest electric utility in Florida and the U.S., and NEER, contracted generation, storage and transmission; Dominion merger signed 2026-05-15, not closed; Q1 IN and Q2 IN on FPL, the deciding part; Q3 for on FPL, against on NEER and the whole; Q4 weighs against; Q5 OUT on integrity, on doubt: campaign-finance and dark-money allegations, a securities class action revived on appeal and settled for $150M, derivative actions naming the CEO settled with political-oversight reforms, all denied; computation only: owner cash $4,191M a year equity-only, range $25.45 to $37.77 vs $81.90, fair $11.53 equity-only, -$33.00 all-equity, no case earns the floor; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: the two-part utility basis, the debt credit with no growth, tax-equity money, Whose tax with renewing credits, the segment measure, Q5 and unresolved litigation)
